questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with warmer weather then in DK. I also wanted to go to a place where I could get a new perspective on my academic learnings so fat. Cape Town was therefore an obvious first choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy to find the information I needed. The most difficult thing was the courses they offered that semester, I figured it out ones I was there, but it was really stressful. The application process was easy but started later than I expected to. 
However, you do need to apply for a visa in quite good time and start preparing for the papers before you know if you have been accepted.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was greeted by two local students that the University of Cape Town International office had arranged to meet the internationals in the airport. I got help to figure out how to read the course list and who to seek out to find if the course was still available. Furthermore, the week before classes started there was an orientation week, where we got a lot of information about UCT, Cape Town, and got to know our classmates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university sent me a list of people I could contact. One of them had available housing. It was Lesley Anne and I can recommend spending the semester at her place. Other international students lived with Mike and they paid a lot of money, for something that was not worth it. Would stay somewhere else. Others found nice housing ones we where there, so that is also a possibility.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is nice to stay relatively close to campus. The areas Observatory, Mowbray, Rondebosch, Rosebank, and Claremont are safe and close to campus. 
Otherwise living in the city is also okay, just be aware that if you are a bachelor students you have to go to campus every day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to registrar online before you come to campus, but if you get declined on some of your classes you have to write to the professors and then they will tell if you can join the class. Then you can apply for that class online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. A little from the international office, but you have to physically go to the different departments to check what classes they offer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: two of the classes I original wanted was not available, but I was satisfied

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will figure it out and most courses are good with highly skilled professors

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some was high, others not so much. It was all fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different in terms of that people used them selves in the classes much more than in DK. In terms off speaking about their own experiences. I kept having a focus on relating it to the readings, and that was very helpful. In most of my courses the level was really high and the professors good. I had one course with mixing level, but I guess that is what you can expect.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANS4405S: Visual Anthropology/Multi-Modal Anthropology

AXL4402S: Thinking Anthropologically

SOC5056S: Political Sociology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
AXL4402S: Thinking Anthropologically
- To learn anthropology from a new perspective and get introduced to other types of readings/theoretics. 
- to go beyond the western world view and learn from a South African perspective   
SOC5056S: Political Sociology
-	One of the best courses I have ever had. Very high level. Difficult but so interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to rent a car, it gives so much freedom! You can also Uber around, which is a bit cheaper, but its not to bad.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets have higher prices than you would expect. It is a lot cheaper to go out, but not so much to make you own (still cheaper than to go out/order all the time)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets have higher prices than you would expect. It is a lot cheaper to go out, but not so much to make you own (still cheaper than to go out/order all the time)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitly join the rowing club, and join as early as possible. Join the mountain and ski club for nice hikes and a good way to get to know some locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely do the Garden Route in the week holiday. I would also visit the Cederberg Mountains and some of the city up north-west.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Cape Town is very westernized

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, and say yes to stuff! annnd go on a festival! and join housing with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The poverty, which is not culture but it was just hard to see and know you could not do much about it

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Peoples kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	You get a unique possibility to do so many outdoor activities, use it!
2.	Cape Town is not a safe safe place, but do not let that scare you. Everything is going to be fine as long as you take your precautions like not going outside when it is dark (take an uber)
3.	Take advantage of the semester and travel a bit after, but remember cape town is sooo fun in December aswell.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the different cafeterias at campus

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing a lot of outdoor activities, most of the time it was between 20-29 degrees which meant that it was possible to do so much, like hiking, going to the beach, running, walking in the forest ect.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The poverty are in some areas very low, which mean that the crime can be very high. The worst thing that happened though was that a lot of my friends got their phone stolen in clubs. But it is the same as in any big city. And cape town is one of the most safe bigger cities in South Africa. 
I found it very exhorting in the end that you constantly had to be fully attentive of your surroundings

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Cape Town and UCT are amazing! Cape Town will forever be in my heart and I will definitly come back

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
